stories.title: Tornado tears through French village, leaving dozens hurt and homes ravaged
stories.summary: A tornado has torn through the French village of Pomas in the country's south-west, injuring 39 people and damaging hundreds of homes. Local authorities said 17 people were taken to hospital. One man said his pregnant wife was injured after their house collapsed on her. More than 120 emergency workers were deployed to the village south of Carcassonne after winds reaching 117km/h (73mph) tore roofs off houses and damaged an estimated 300 homes on Monday. "Half the village has been destroyed," said one resident called Pierre, who described the tornado as swirling like a "huge red and yellow chimney". "There's a huge castle and a third of it is has collapsed - even though these are stones that have stood for 1,000 years," Pierre told Ici Occitanie. The extreme weather has left about 2,800 homes across 10 villages without electricity, according to officials. Local sub-prefect Emmanuelle Plantier-Lemarchand told French radio that she was not aware of anyone missing. She lowered the number of victims from 41 to 39, and said 15 of them had been treated in hospital. "I heard this massive noise... then I saw everything flying around in the air and my roof collapsed," shocked resident Chantal told French radio. "I've got no house left, that's for sure."

stories.title: NATO remains hostile bloc for Russia, continues to expand — Medvedev
stories.summary: The politician stressed that Moscow needed guarantees from NATO that no other states would attack Russia and that all hostile actions against the country would cease
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 25.
NATO remains a hostile military-political alliance for Russia and continues to expand, Russian Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev said in an interview with Yuzhnaya Ossetia newspaper.
"This hostile military-political bloc not only continues to exist but is constantly expanding.
NATO plans to admit new members from former Soviet republics, including Georgia and Ukraine.
How should we respond?
It is quite clear that such moves pose an existential threat to Russia," Medvedev said.
He stressed that Moscow only needs guarantees from NATO that no other states will attack Russia and that all hostile actions against the country will cease.

stories.title: Can ‘One Nation, One Election’ happen in 2029? Opposition raises constitutional concerns
stories.summary: The Centre’s ‘One Nation, One Election’ proposal has sparked a debate over simultaneous Lok Sabha and State Assembly polls. JPC chairman P.P. Chaudhary says the move is feasible with political will and constitutional changes, while Congress leader P. Chidambaram has argued that the proposed legislation violates the basic structure of the Constitution.

stories.title: Kremlin calls rumors about mobilization in Russia fake news spread by Kiev
stories.summary: Dmitry Peskov stressed that the Kiev regime attempted to ideologically destabilize the situation in Russia
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 25.
Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov called rumors about alleged mobilization in Russia a newspaper hoax deliberately circulated by the Ukrainian government.
"You know, Ukrainian authorities spread all of that.
Naturally, the [Kiev] regime is attempting to ideologically destabilize the situation in our country.
These are all newspaper hoaxes deliberately planted in the media," the Kremlin spokesman told RTVI.
Earlier, Vladimir Zelensky repeatedly claimed that Russian authorities would declare new mobilization this fall.
Ukrainian media also circulated these rumors.
